problem: Improve a small classifier on sklearn.load_digits (1797 handwritten8x8 digit images) under label-preserving corruptions: additive pixel noise and random pixel dropout. Use fixed stratified train/validation/test split, fit preprocessing on train only, reserve test for final evaluation, and compare a standardized RBF-SVM plus ordinary corruption augmentation. Optimize mean accuracy across clean and fixed corruption severities under 5 CPU minutes on an Apple Silicon laptop, no pretrained models or external data. Propose a distinct implementable intervention and ablation; do not merely list known techniques or claim external novelty.

proposal.title: Severity-Swept Augmentation for Corruption-Robust Digit Classification
proposal.intervention: Construct an augmented training set by applying additive Gaussian noise and random pixel dropout at K discrete severity levels drawn from a sinusoidal sweep across [0,1], then train a single RBF-SVM on the concatenation of clean plus all augmented copies. Scaler is fit once on clean training pixels only; all augmented copies are transformed under that fixed scaler before concatenation.
proposal.mechanism: A uniform severity grid over-represents mid-range corruptions relative to the extremes when the corruption function is nonlinear in severity. The sinusoidal schedule spends equal arc-length at low, mid, and high severities, ensuring the SVM margin is shaped by support-vector candidates from the full corruption spectrum. This should reduce accuracy degradation at high-severity test conditions without sacrificing clean accuracy.
proposal.assumptions: The corruption function is sufficiently nonlinear in severity that uniform sampling creates an imbalanced effective distribution of corrupted feature vectors. The RBF-SVM has enough capacity to absorb the expanded training set within the time budget. Augmented copies generated from pre-scaler pixel space and then scaled are representative of test-time corrupted inputs, which are also scaled under the same fixed scaler.
proposal.baseline: Same pipeline with uniform severity schedule: phases replaced by K equally spaced values in [0,1], producing identical total sample count. All other hyperparameters, seeds, and evaluation corruptions are held fixed.
proposal.metric: Mean classification accuracy across four fixed test conditions: clean, low-severity, medium-severity, and high-severity corruption, evaluated on a held-out stratified test split never seen during fitting or augmentation design.
proposal.falsification: Replace the sinusoidal schedule with a constant mid-severity schedule (all K phases set to 0.5). If the sinusoidal sweep provides no benefit, mean test accuracy will be statistically indistinguishable from or better than the swept version. This requires changing one line and re-running, completing well within two minutes. A further check: set K=1 (single augmentation pass at mid-severity) to confirm that any gain from the sweep is not simply explained by increased training set size.
proposal.implementation:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import load_digits
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedShuffleSplit
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.svm import SVC
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score

digits = load_digits()
X, y = digits.data / 16.0, digits.target

sss = StratifiedShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
tv_idx, test_idx = next(sss.split(X, y))
sss2 = StratifiedShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=0.25, random_state=42)
train_idx, val_idx = next(sss2.split(X[tv_idx], y[tv_idx]))
train_idx = tv_idx[train_idx]

X_tr, y_tr = X[train_idx], y[train_idx]
X_te, y_te = X[test_idx], y[test_idx]

scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X_tr)
X_tr_s = scaler.transform(X_tr)
X_te_s = scaler.transform(X_te)

def corrupt(X, sigma, p, rng):
    out = X + rng.normal(0, sigma, X.shape)
    out[rng.random(X.shape) < p] = 0.0
    return np.clip(out, 0, 1)

K = 8
phases = [0.5*(1 + np.sin(2*np.pi*i/K)) for i in range(K)]  # swap to [0.5]*K for ablation
rng_aug = np.random.default_rng(0)
parts, labels = [X_tr_s], [y_tr]
for s in phases:
    parts.append(scaler.transform(corrupt(X_tr, 0.5*s, 0.15*s, rng_aug)))
    labels.append(y_tr)
X_aug, y_aug = np.vstack(parts), np.concatenate(labels)

svm = SVC(kernel='rbf', C=10, gamma='scale').fit(X_aug, y_aug)

rng_te = np.random.default_rng(99)
for sig, p, name in [(0,0,'clean'),(0.2,0.05,'low'),(0.4,0.10,'med'),(0.6,0.15,'high')]:
    Xc = scaler.transform(corrupt(X_te, sig, p, rng_te)) if sig > 0 else X_te_s
    print(f"{name}: {accuracy_score(y_te, svm.predict(Xc)):.3f}")
